x: Ian Badiali could only finish 4th in the 440 final which was won in 50.7 secs, and it is a pity that we are forced to run Ian at this distance as we think he prefers the half-mile. Bill Lucas set up yet another "meet" record with his time of 14 min. 30.6 secs. in the 3 miles run, and he beat Alec Olney and K.
Bill Lucas then took us to the front on the third stage but Vern Blowfield could not hold Alec Olney over the final "leg," and so we finished 2nd to Thames Valley H.
On the first stage from Mitcham to Purley we had Jack Brown, and he put up a truly magnificent performance to beat Alec Olney’s record time of 27.37 by five seconds.
Although there was a strong wind blowing the weather was fine, and Alec Olney beat his old record by 3 seconds, with a time of 49 mins. 40 secs.

However even Driver's time was not unbeatable, for first Jim Peters lowered it by 10 seconds and in doing so passed Charlie Walker and took Essex Beagles into 2nd place, and later by Alec Olney who reduced it by another 7 seconds without bringing his club T.V.H. anywhere near the front.

Our new Cross Country Captain, Eddie Short, then took over at Purley for the long grind to Earlswood and I suppose no one could wish for a less envious task than to chase Alec Olney of T.V.H. who must be considered one of the best road runners of all time.

They were followed in by the T.V.H. star Alec Olney and another young rising luminary Walter Hesketh from Manchester A.C. Lancashire were clear in the team championship with a fifty points margin over Warwickshire.
Willie Slykhuis must be favourite surely and Alec Olney was already making a name for himself. I decided to back Bill for 3rd (one of my class-mates had decided to run a book this year).
Gordon Pirie, Frank Sando, Alec Olney, John Parlett, Chris Chataway … these are just some of the stars of the ’50s & ’60s with whom Charlie tangled with over track, road and cross country.
